explain.say: A giraffe's brain sits about two metres above its heart, so its heart must push blood uphill all the way. To do it, giraffes have blood pressure about twice as high as ours.

faq.q: How big is a giraffe's heart?
faq.a: A giraffe's heart can weigh about 11 kilograms. Surprisingly, compared with its body it is about the same size as other mammals' hearts; its strength comes from a very thick left ventricle wall.
asks: Why does a giraffe need a strong heart?
How high is giraffe blood pressure?

faq.q: How does blood get up a giraffe's neck?
faq.a: The heart pumps at about twice our blood pressure, enough to lift blood two metres to the brain. Thick-walled arteries in the neck cope with that pressure without bursting.
asks: How does a giraffe's heart reach its head?
Why do giraffe arteries have thick walls?

faq.q: Why don't giraffes faint when they bend down?
faq.a: Valves in the jugular veins stop blood flowing back down into the head, and the blood vessels quickly adjust the flow. So the giraffe can lower its head to drink and lift it again without fainting.
asks: What happens when a giraffe drinks?
What do the valves in a giraffe's neck do?

faq.q: Why don't giraffes' legs swell up?
faq.a: With such high blood pressure, fluid would leak into the legs. A giraffe's legs have tight skin and tough tissue that act like compression socks, squeezing fluid back. Pilots' pressure suits use the same idea.
asks: Do giraffes wear natural compression socks?
How do giraffe legs cope with pressure?

faq.q: How long is a giraffe's neck?
faq.a: A giraffe's neck can be about two metres long, yet it has just seven neck bones, the same number as a human. Each bone can be over 25 centimetres long.
asks: How many bones are in a giraffe's neck?
Why do giraffes have long necks?

facts: A giraffe's blood pressure is roughly twice that of a human, high enough to push blood about two metres up to the brain.
A giraffe has seven neck vertebrae, the same number as humans.
